$comment: An entry is permitted only where the banned phrasing is TRUE as written: a fact about a
third party's licence, or a contrastive sentence that explains why Eustress is not on those
terms. No entry here describes Eustress's own licence. Eustress is source-available under
The ceiling is 6 entries and every entry needs a reason of at least 20 characters. Entries
match on path + line + exact text, so if the line is edited the entry stops matching and the
hit resurfaces for a fresh decision. That is deliberate.

entries.reason: Contrastive heading on the licence page: it names the alternative in order to explain why Eustress is source-available under PolyForm Shield instead. Removing it would delete the explanation, not a claim.
Describes the licensing of two third-party FBX libraries the pipeline could adopt. True about fbxcel; says nothing about the Eustress licence.

entries.text: FBX licensing path (Autodesk SDK / open source)?
entries.reason: An open engineering question about which third-party FBX SDK to license. It is about Autodesk's terms, not about the terms Eustress is offered on.

entries.text: (MIT-licensed; same project ownership and release cadence)
entries.reason: States the actual licence of the rojo-rbx crates the importer depends on. That fact is accurate and is exactly what a dependency-licence review needs to read.

entries.text: MinIO is an open-source, S3-compatible object storage.
entries.reason: MinIO is a third-party storage server and the sentence is true about MinIO. Rewording it would make the self-hosting guide wrong about the software it is recommending.

entries.text: MinIO is an open-source, S3-compatible object storage server.
entries.reason: The same true statement about the third-party MinIO server, in the module docs of the S3 asset backend that talks to it.
